intended_object: For a finite family of pairwise commuting endomorphisms p_i of an R-module M and a sign pattern ε : I → Bool, the joint projector ∏_i q_i, where q_i = p_i if ε_i is true and q_i = 1 − p_i otherwise. For idempotent p_i this is the projection onto the block ⋂_{ε_i} range p_i ∩ ⋂_{¬ε_i} ker p_i. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the lemmas `range_jointProjector` and `jointProjectors_completeOrthogonalIdempotents`.
explanation:
The body is `Finset.univ.noncommProd (fun i ↦ if ε i then p i else 1 - p i)`, taken over a `Fintype` instance chosen from `Finite I`. The commutativity side condition comes from `jointFactors_pairwise`. Because the factors commute, `noncommProd` gives the product independently of the enumeration (`jointProjector_eq_noncommProd`). So this is exactly the product of p_i at the true bits and 1 − p_i at the false bits.

Degenerate cases behave correctly. For empty I the product is 1, matching the whole-module block ⊤. The Pairwise hypothesis is only needed for i ≠ j, which is all that `noncommProd` uses.

The library proves what the intended object should satisfy:
- for idempotent p_i, the range of the projector is the joint range/kernel block;
- the projectors over all ε form a complete orthogonal family of idempotents.

Generality is good. R is only a semiring and M is any additive commutative group with an R-module structure; the group structure is needed to form 1 − p_i in the endomorphism ring. Abstractly, the same product makes sense in any ring with commuting elements. But the object here is a "projector", meant to cut a module into range/kernel blocks, so stating it in `Module.End R M` matches its role. Mathlib has no general Boolean-pattern product of commuting idempotents; `Mathlib/RingTheory/Idempotents.lean` has only related lemmas such as `∏ (1 - e i)`. So there is no broader Mathlib notion that this definition duplicates.
